title: spec review: S3: dynamic skill disclosure in shadow: per worker spawn compute the smallest useful skill set (deterministic candidates → cap), log it as the skill_selection decision next to the static exposure, measure the token delta; exposure unchanged (v2)
spec:
Program brief .orchestrator/roadmap-skills.md P8 (steps 1-4 and 7), P10, P29, P30 (P37 stage 3). Depends on T-0894 (skill telemetry: skills_exposed/skills_used/skill tokens in run context, skill_selection decision rows, skill_scorecard) and T-0867 (skills_registry.candidates(task, role), render(id, level), compact skills with declared triggers/task_classes/tools/requires_context). Facts: exposure today is static (all active registry skills for the role); the context program's promotion.mode() reads per-feature modes from pool.toml; decision_log kind skill_selection exists after S1b.
Do:
1. pool.toml: add `[skills] mode = "shadow"` (off | shadow | active; dated comment; revert: off) and `max_selected = 3`; promotion.FEATURES gains "skill_routing" (table skills, key mode, default shadow) with an evidence loader returning n = skill_selection rows carrying a minimal set (stay until Stage 4 scorecards provide quality deltas).
2. orchestrator/skill_router.py (new): `select(task, role, cfg=None, history=None) -> {"candidates": [...], "selected": [ids], "rejected": [{"id", "reason"}], "reason", "tokens_exposed_l0", "tokens_selected_l0", "tokens_selected_l2", "ambiguous": [ids]}`. Deterministic rules: role-only skills that the role's prompt relies on are mandatory (implement-spec for executors, adversarial-review for review/spec_review, challenge for challenge, memory + orchestrate + resume + write-spec for planner, repo-map/test-gap/trace-callers only when their triggers match, classify/compact-memory only for triage); trigger matches from skills_registry.candidates rank next; cap at max_selected keeping mandatory first; candidates with a single weak trigger match (one keyword) go to "ambiguous" (reserved for Jev in Stage 9) and are excluded from selected in shadow; `history` (Stage 4 scorecard rows) is accepted but unused until Stage 4 fills it. Never returns an empty set for a role that has a mandatory skill.
3. Shadow wiring: in spawn.run_worker and the Codex dispatch path, when [skills] mode is shadow or active (active treated as shadow with a one-time notify warning until Stage 5), call skill_router.select and (a) extend the skill_selection decision row from S1b: candidates = registry ids for the role, deterministic = {"triggers": matched per candidate, "task_class", "mandatory": ids}, selected = the minimal set, rejected = the rest with reasons, extra = {"tokens_exposed_l0", "tokens_selected_l0", "tokens_selected_l2", "ambiguous"}, mode = the mode; (b) add skills_selected and skill_tokens_selected_l0/l2 to packet_meta so bus.log_run carries them (bus.py copied keys). Worker exposure stays the static set; nothing in .claude/skills, prompts or AGENTS.md changes.
4. Recovery signal (P30 skill recovery rate): after completion, compare skills_used (S1b) with skills_selected: a used skill that was not selected is a "skill_recovery"; record it in decision_log.outcome for the skill_selection row and count it in skill_scorecard as skill_recovery_rate per role (recoveries / spawns with a selection). Also skill_reduction = 1 - tokens_selected_l0 / tokens_exposed_l0 per role.
5. `orchestrator scorecard --skills` shows selected-set size avg, skill_reduction and skill_recovery_rate; `--economy` skills block includes them. docs/skill-intelligence/04-routing.md (≤60 lines): the rules, mandatory table, what shadow logs, what active will do (Stage 5), revert path.
Tests (unittest): tests/test_skill_router.py::test_executor_gets_implement_spec_mandatory_and_nothing_irrelevant, ::test_scout_who_calls_task_selects_trace_callers_not_repo_map, ::test_cap_keeps_mandatory_first, ::test_single_weak_match_goes_to_ambiguous_not_selected, ::test_never_empty_for_roles_with_mandatory; tests/test_spawn.py::test_skill_selection_row_and_meta_in_shadow_without_exposure_change (exposure list identical to mode off; decision row carries selected and rejected); tests/test_skill_scorecard.py::test_skill_recovery_rate_and_reduction. Never quote double-brace placeholder tokens literally. Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result.

SPEC v2 (2026-09-23 04:30) after spec review T-0909 (request_changes), binding on top of v1:
- pool.toml: add the keys `mode = "shadow"` and `max_selected = 3` to the EXISTING [skills] table (created by the discovery task: trusted_repos, allowed_domains); never declare the table twice.
- The cap applies to non-mandatory candidates only: mandatory skills for the role are always all selected (planner has four), then up to max_selected further candidates by trigger strength.
- "Weak match" is defined by trigger strength, not by count: strength = number of words in the matched trigger phrase(s) summed over matches; a candidate whose total strength is 1 (a single one-word trigger such as "impact") is ambiguous; a multi-word phrase such as "who calls" has strength 2 and is a firm match. test_scout_who_calls_task_selects_trace_callers_not_repo_map therefore holds.
- promotion.collect(): a new `if feature == "skill_routing":` branch counts skill_selection decision rows whose mode is shadow or active AND whose reason is not the stage-1 static reason (reason != "stage1 static"), so the legacy full-exposure rows are excluded; test tests/test_promotion.py::test_skill_routing_evidence_excludes_static_rows.
acceptance: pool.toml has [skills] mode = "shadow" and promotion.FEATURES has skill_routing; docs/skill-intelligence/04-routing.md exists; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

risks.issue: Spec's '## existing tests' table marks this file (and tests/test_spawn.py, tests/test_promotion.py) as 'missing', but all three already exist with real passing suites (test_skill_scorecard.py has SkillScorecardTests with test_use_rate_and_overhead_ratio_per_skill and test_skill_tokens_per_accepted_task). tests-green.sh runs the whole tests/ directory via unittest discover, not just the acceptance-named ids, but it also does not assert that pre-existing test methods remain present -- so an executor that trusts the stale 'missing' label and recreates/overwrites the file instead of appending a method to the existing TestCase class would silently delete existing coverage and the gate would not catch it.

skill_router.select()'s 'tokens_exposed_l0' (used for skill_reduction = 1 - tokens_selected_l0/tokens_exposed_l0 in step 5) is not pinned to a specific baseline. The existing stage-1 exposure computed in spawn.py's _skill_exposure and executor.py's _codex_skill_meta sums tokens across ALL active builtin registry skills regardless of role (matching what the shared .claude/skills directory actually shows the worker), whereas step 2 defines candidates as 'registry ids for the role' (a much smaller, role-filtered set). Depending on which figure the router reports as tokens_exposed_l0, skill_reduction will differ by roughly an order of magnitude and mean different things (true context savings vs. role-relevance savings). No listed acceptance test pins the exact value, so this ambiguity won't fail a test, but it will produce an economy metric whose meaning is unclear when Stage 5 promotion decisions later read it.

suggested_spec_changes: Add to step 3 (or the conditional instructions): when adding tests/test_skill_scorecard.py::test_skill_recovery_rate_and_reduction and any new tests/test_spawn.py / tests/test_promotion.py methods, append to the existing SkillScorecardTests / existing TestCase classes in those files -- do not recreate or overwrite them; correct the '## existing tests' table entries for tests/test_skill_scorecard.py, tests/test_spawn.py, and tests/test_promotion.py from 'missing' to 'present'.

In step 2, state explicitly whether skill_router.select()'s tokens_exposed_l0 is the role-filtered candidate token sum (registry ids for the role) or the full static cross-role exposure sum that _skill_exposure/_codex_skill_meta already compute, so skill_reduction in step 5 has one unambiguous baseline.
